name: Political instability
value: Indonesia VP succession; no G20 collapse
summary: Indonesia's vice-president has resigned amid an impeachment push; parties leave Prabowo to pick a successor
state: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned, as reported on 11 Nov, over a dispute about his eligibility (New Straits Times). More than 100 lawmakers from all eight House parties signed a petition saying he no longer meets the requirements for office, and House leadership sent it to a plenary on 12 Nov (Jakarta Post). The People's Consultative Assembly will choose a successor from the president's nominees. This is a constitutional succession, not a government collapse, and searches on 15 Nov found no G20 coup or contested election.
for_you: No direct effect on UK residents. Travellers to Indonesia can follow FCDO travel advice for any changes around political events.
rubric_hit: Normal: no G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in past month; Indonesia VP change is a constitutional succession

why: Coups, contested elections and constitutional crises in large economies unsettle markets, alliances and policy.

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.

rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.
